verses.english: Linked Discourses 22.36
4. It’s Not Yours
A Mendicant (2nd)
At Sāvatthī.

verses.pali: Atha kho aññataro bhikkhu yena bhagavā …pe… ekamantaṁ nisinno kho so bhikkhu bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then a mendicant went up to the Buddha … and asked him,

verses.pali: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā saṅkhittena dhammaṁ desetu yamahaṁ bhagavato dhammaṁ sutvā eko vūpakaṭṭho appamatto ātāpī pahitatto vihareyyan”ti.
verses.english: “Sir, may the Buddha please teach me Dhamma in brief. When I’ve heard it, I’ll live alone, withdrawn, diligent, keen, and resolute.”
“Mendicant, you’re measured against what you have an underlying tendency for,
and you’re reckoned by what you’re measured against.
You’re not measured against what you have no underlying tendency for,

verses.pali: yaṁ nānumīyati na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchatī”ti.
verses.english: and you’re not reckoned by what you’re not measured against.”
“Understood, Blessed One! Understood, Holy One!”

verses.pali: “Yathā kathaṁ pana tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāsī”ti?
verses.english: “But how do you see the detailed meaning of my brief statement?”
“If you have an underlying tendency for form, you’re measured against that,
and you’re reckoned by what you’re measured against.
If you have an underlying tendency for feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness, you’re measured against that,
and you’re reckoned by what you’re measured against.

verses.pali: Rūpañce, bhante, nānuseti na taṁ anumīyati;
verses.english: If you have no underlying tendency for form, you’re not measured against that,

verses.pali: yaṁ nānumīyati na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: and you’re not reckoned by what you’re not measured against.
If you have no underlying tendency for feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness, you’re not measured against that,

verses.pali: yaṁ nānumīyati na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: and you’re not reckoned by what you’re not measured against.

verses.pali: Imassa khvāhaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāmī”ti.
verses.english: That’s how I understand the detailed meaning of the Buddha’s brief statement.”
“Good, good, mendicant!

verses.pali: Sādhu kho tvaṁ, bhikkhu, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa vitthārena atthaṁ ājānāsi.
verses.english: It’s good that you understand the detailed meaning of what I’ve said in brief like this.
If you have an underlying tendency for form, you’re measured against that,
and you’re reckoned by what you’re measured against.
If you have an underlying tendency for feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness, you’re measured against that,
and you’re reckoned by what you’re measured against.

verses.pali: Rūpañce, bhikkhu, nānuseti na taṁ anumīyati;
verses.english: If you have no underlying tendency for form, you’re not measured against that,

verses.pali: yaṁ nānumīyati na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: and you’re not reckoned by what you’re not measured against.
If you have no underlying tendency for feeling …
perception …
choices …
consciousness, you’re not measured against that,

verses.pali: yaṁ nānumīyati na tena saṅkhaṁ gacchati.
verses.english: and you’re not reckoned by what you’re not measured against.

verses.pali: Imassa kho, bhikkhu, mayā saṅkhittena bhāsitassa evaṁ vitthārena attho daṭṭhabbo”ti …pe…
verses.english: This is how to understand the detailed meaning of what I said in brief.” …

verses.pali: aññataro ca pana so bhikkhu arahataṁ ahosīti.
verses.english: And that mendicant became one of the perfected.
